chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

The pillar of man is the intellect, and from the intellect come insightfulness, understanding, memorization, and knowledge; and through the intellect he becomes complete — it is his guide, his insight, and the key to his affairs.

So when the support of his intellect is from the light, he would be a scholar, a memorizer, oft-remembering of God, discerning, and understanding. Thus he would know how, and why, and where; and he would recognize who counseled him sincerely and who deceived him.
So when he recognizes that, he recognizes its course, its connections and its disconnections, and he dedicates the oneness of God sincerely and the acknowledgement of obedience.

So when he does that, he would be a recoverer of what was missed and would anticipate what is coming; he knows what he is in, and for what reason he is here, and from where it comes to him, and toward what he is heading — and all of that is from the support of the intellect.

key_terms.الْعَقْل: Intellect/reason (aql) — in Shia theology, one of the two greatest proofs (hujja) alongside the prophets and Imams
key_terms.الْفِطْنَة: Perceptiveness/sharpness of mind — one of four faculties derived from the intellect
key_terms.الْوَحْدَانِيَّة: Divine oneness/uniqueness (tawhid) — the foundational monotheistic creed
key_terms.تَأْيِيد: Divine support/reinforcement — specifically the light (nur) from God that strengthens the intellect
key_terms.دِعَامَة: Pillar, foundation, structural support — used metaphorically for the foundational role of intellect

ai.seo_question: What is the role of intellect (aql) in Islamic spirituality according to Imam Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) presents the intellect (aql) as the foundational pillar of human existence, from which all cognitive and spiritual faculties derive. He outlines a progressive model in which an intellect divinely supported by light (nur) elevates a person to become a true scholar and seeker of God, capable of moral discernment and eschatological awareness. This teaching was addressed to students of the Imami tradition seeking to understand why the intellect is considered the first proof (hujja) in Shia theology.
